name: Chesapeake
card: 7,291 sales in 24 months, median $420,000 – South Norfolk, Riverwalk, Greenbrier, Deep Creek, Great Bridge and more.
description: Chesapeake VA neighborhood guides and homes for sale from Chris Jenkins of Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group. Buyer and seller help across Chesapeake.
lede: Chesapeake is an independent city in southeastern Virginia, bordering Norfolk, Portsmouth, Suffolk and Virginia Beach and the North Carolina line. Chris Jenkins, a Hampton Roads native and REALTOR® with Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group, walks you through Chesapeake one neighborhood at a time.
tldr: Chesapeake, VA is a Hampton Roads city made up of distinct sections such as Great Bridge, Deep Creek, Greenbrier, Western Branch, Indian River and South Norfolk. Chris Jenkins, a Chesapeake real estate agent with Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group, helps buyers and sellers across all of them.

sections.html:
Chesapeake is not one single market. Home shoppers usually think in terms of its sections: Great Bridge in the central part of the city, Deep Creek and the Grassfield area to the south, Greenbrier around the Battlefield Boulevard and Greenbrier Parkway corridors, Western Branch toward Portsmouth and Suffolk, and Indian River and South Norfolk closer to Norfolk. Each has its own mix of home ages, lot sizes, association fees and commute patterns, which is why a neighborhood-level guide matters more than a citywide average.

Chris Jenkins has represented buyers and sellers in many of these areas, including Greenbrier East, Great Bridge and Indian River, according to client reviews on his reviews section.

sections.h2: Chesapeake Home Prices: What Sold in the Last 24 Months
sections.html:
REIN MLS records show 7,291 closed residential sales in Chesapeake between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026. The citywide median sold price was $420,000, the median home took 18 days to sell, and the median price per square foot was $219. Those citywide numbers hide big differences between neighborhoods: the median in Riverwalk was $281,750, while in Hickory it was $717,500. That is why each guide below shows the numbers for its own community.

Chris Jenkins of Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group uses closed-sale data like this, not asking prices, to price homes for sellers and to guide buyers on what a fair offer looks like.

What is the median home price in Chesapeake VA?

REIN MLS shows a median sold price of $420,000 across 7,291 closed residential sales in Chesapeake between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026, with a median of 18 days on market. Prices vary a lot by neighborhood, so ask Chris Jenkins for the numbers in your community.
What are the main areas of Chesapeake, Virginia?

Common ways to describe Chesapeake are Great Bridge, Deep Creek, Greenbrier, Western Branch, Indian River and South Norfolk. Each section differs in home age, lot size, association dues and commute, so ask Chris Jenkins to compare the exact neighborhoods you are considering.
Are there waterfront homes in Chesapeake?
Yes, parts of Chesapeake have waterfront and water-view homes, but flood-zone status and insurance cost vary from lot to lot. Chris Jenkins checks flood zones with you before you make an offer.
